sourceBindings.text: Separate written case: corn
Corn case: pH 5.4 (stated target 6.0–7.0), OM 2.0% (stated target >3%), N Low, P Low, K Optimum; compacted soil and prior yellow leaves.
Explain the supplied categories simply and clearly identify them as provided.
List conditional next actions for lime requirement, nutrient interpretation, compaction/drainage and crop check in defensible order.
Prior yellow leaves do not independently prove N deficiency; no method, rate or date may be invented.
This corn exercise is separate from the West Field tomato report.

An average summarizes separate measurements; it does not manufacture a new physical measurement.

A polished product still needs a verified trainer review and sound recommendation.

sourceBindings.text: Keep later written cases distinct

Case A: pH 5.2, N Low, P Low, K Medium, OM 1%, with two soil techniques and crop examples requested. Case B: pH 6.8, N Medium, P High, K Low, requesting a seasonal fertilizer strategy and two suitable crops.
Retain each exact dataset and requested number of techniques or crops.

For case A, assess a crop-specific lime requirement and a method-calibrated N/P/OM plan as two distinct pathways. Broccoli and common beans are examples at risk under the starting pH 5.2 because extension growing guidance prefers about pH 6–7; this is a risk hypothesis, not a guaranteed failure. After verified improvement, tomatoes and sweet corn are two candidate crops if climate, drainage, salinity, nutrient balance and local variety requirements also fit.

For case B, avoid an unnecessary P input, investigate the reported K shortage by method and crop need, and balance N from all sources. Tomatoes and sweet corn could be investigated as candidates at pH 6.8, but the incomplete case does not prove their suitability or set a K rate.
Question prompts and requested crop examples are preserved while crop success remains conditional on actual site evidence.
